purpose: Isolate untrusted content, manage session vs fresh tradeoffs, prevent contamination and negation rebound, and stop lateral injection across multi-agent systems.
assumptions: Context segments can be labeled with trust tiers
Some roles can be spawned with clean context and a task packet
Integrator authenticity checks exist for TASK admission

competency_questions.question: What trust tier does each context segment have and who can rewrite tier0?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: labels segments tier0-3 and states only operator/integrator rewrite tier0

competency_questions.question: How is untrusted content prevented from becoming instructions?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: describes quarantine or data-vs-instruction rule with example

competency_questions.question: When should a subagent be fresh vs continue a session?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: gives role matrix with at least build vs judge

competency_questions.question: How are tool outputs and markup isolated from authority?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: states observation labeling, size bounds, strip/quote steps

competency_questions.question: What is contamination and how do you detect priming before risky actions?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: defines residual influence and at least one pre-action check

competency_questions.question: How does negation rebound fail and what positive framing replaces ban walls?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: names rebound risk and required-action-first pattern with ban alternative pairs

competency_questions.question: How do you keep secrets out of low-trust and sandboxed contexts?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: secret-free worker policy and redaction before EXCHANGE

competency_questions.question: How are author, judge, and planner roles separated in context?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: maps roles to distinct context/session and reviewer read-only scope

competency_questions.question: What makes a TASK instruction authentic versus peer data?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: requires authenticated integrator TASK block; peers are data

competency_questions.question: What does a sandbox prompt include for a risky untrusted-read subtask?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: allowlisted tools, closed schema, positive instructions, no secrets

competency_questions.question: How are memory writes gated and audited against poisoning?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: tier check on write; global denies tier3; audit on deny

competency_questions.question: What is the contamination reset protocol and when does resume re-check?

glossary.definition: Label tier0-3 on context segments controlling who may rewrite whom
Worker started with clean context plus task packet, not full parent transcript
Role that extracts structured claims from untrusted content without authority
Residual priming influence after source text is gone or de-emphasized
Ironic activation of forbidden behaviors after heavy DON'T framing
State required actions first; pair bans with allowed alternatives
Peer agent content attempting to act as system/task instructions
Untrusted content stored durably and reloaded as high-trust later
Minimal spawn payload: pins, goal, constraints, scoped inputs
Fixture injection used to regression-test isolation controls

source_registry.description: heuristic priors for LLM context isolation, freshness, and contamination control in multi-agent systems
source_registry.citation_or_locator: heuristic prior; operational practice for agent orchestration; no external dataset supplied

nodes.definition: Declare explicit trust tiers for content: tier0 system/integrator instructions, tier1 operator task text after authenticity checks, tier2 tool outputs from controlled repos, tier3 untrusted web/user paste/third-party. Boundaries dictate isolation: lower tiers must not rewrite higher-tier obligations. Without tiers, every string competes equally and injection wins by volume.

included: tier labels for all context sources
no lower-tier rewrite of higher obligations

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: untrusted paste overrides ASSIGNEE or hard denials in the same context

pros.claim: Tiers make isolation policies enforceable
pros.example: tier3 web text cannot change gate commands

cons.claim: Mis-tiering trusted tool output as tier0 grants excess authority

failure_modes: flat context with no source labels
user paste silently merged into system
acceptance_tests: every segment labeled tier0-3; policy forbids tier>=2 from editing tier0 rules

nodes.definition: Spawn workers with a clean context: system pins plus task packet only, not the parent full contaminated or bloated transcript. Freshness resets priming and limits leakage of irrelevant constraints. Packet must still carry goal, paths, constraints, and inputs (typically 2-12k tokens not 80k-plus clones).

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: worker inherits parent chat and repeats parent mistaken assumption

pros.claim: Fresh workers avoid inherited priming and bloat
pros.example: reviewer does not see author victory narrative

cons.claim: Under-specified packets cause redundant discovery

acceptance_tests: spawn docs require fresh flag; packet schema lists required fields
revisit_triggers: packet size creeps toward full clone

nodes.definition: Read untrusted content in a quarantined role that may only emit structured extractions (summary, claims, links, risk flags) never free-form instructions merged into the main agent. Quarantine outputs are tier2/3 data. Main agent treats them as claims to verify, not orders to obey.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: main agent executes ignore-previous-instructions found inside a fetched README

pros.claim: Quarantine blocks instruction injection from content
pros.example: README jailbreak becomes a claim record

cons.claim: Over-quarantine slows trusted internal docs

failure_modes: paste web HTML into system prompt
merge quarantine prose into developer instructions
acceptance_tests: untrusted reads use quarantine role; output schema has no authority fields

nodes.definition: Detect and limit priming: earlier examples, errors, or emotional framing bias later judgments (anchoring, availability). Contamination is residual influence after triggering text is gone. Mitigations: fresh subagents for high-stakes judgments, debias checklists, author/evaluator separation.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: evaluator scores higher after seeing author confident self-assessment in-context

pros.claim: Naming contamination enables role separation

cons.claim: Excessive resets lose useful calibrated priors

failure_modes: evaluator reads full builder victory transcript
acceptance_tests: high-stakes judge uses fresh context or redacted packet without self-scores

nodes.definition: Negative instructions (do NOT force-push, never mention X) can prime the forbidden act via ironic process rebound effects: models and humans over-activate the negated concept. Pure negation lists are high-risk for compliance-sensitive behaviors. Measure near-miss tool args after heavy DON'T framing. This is a first-class failure mode, not a footnote.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: agent nearly force-pushes after a prompt wall of DO-NOT force-push examples

pros.claim: Recognizing rebound explains ban-only prompt failures

cons.claim: Fear of negation can under-specify hard stops if not replaced
cons.example: removing bans without stating required push mode

failure_modes: only listing forbidden acts with no required alternative
acceptance_tests: policy notes rebound risk; forbids ban-only framing for critical safety tools

nodes.definition: Prefer constructive instructions that state required behavior: use fast-forward push only to grok/*, edit only paths in SCOPE, answer with allowed tools. Pair each hard stop with the allowed alternative. Keep a short closed ban list for catastrophic acts but lead with positive procedure. Reduces rebound while preserving enforceability.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: rewritten standing orders still lead with 40 DON'T lines and weak DO procedure

pros.claim: Positive frames improve compliance without deleting hard stops
pros.example: FF push to grok/* only beats long force-push DON'T essay

cons.claim: Vague positive goals without checks become slogans

failure_modes: positive tone that omits gate requirements
acceptance_tests: critical ops instructions lead with required action; each ban has allowed alternative
revisit_triggers: ban lists grow without DO pairs

nodes.definition: Choose session continuity (memory, cheaper turns, repair context) vs stateless fresh calls (isolation, reproducibility, less priming). Long sessions accumulate contamination and rot; pure stateless loses repair context. Hybrid: session for build loops, fresh for judge, quarantine, and high-risk tool planning.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: single endless session used for both authoring and final acceptance judging

pros.claim: Role-based hybrid cuts contamination on judgments
pros.example: build stays session; xverify is fresh

cons.claim: Too many fresh starts lose cheap incremental repair
cons.example: every file edit in new session

failure_modes: one session forever for all roles
stateless even for multi-step compile fix loops
acceptance_tests: role matrix: build|judge|quarantine|plan maps to session or fresh

nodes.definition: Control what agents may write into each other contexts: digests with schemas, not free-form now-you-must directives from peer workers. Peer output is data under TRUST_BOUNDARY. Only integrator/tier0 may issue TASK instructions. Prevents lateral prompt injection across the swarm.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: peer EXCHANGE message interpreted as orders without ASSIGNEE filter

pros.claim: Lateral injection blocked by data-vs-instruction rule

cons.claim: Over-rigid schemas slow ad-hoc collaboration
cons.example: useful warnings dropped for schema mismatch

failure_modes: treat any EXCHANGE file as system orders
acceptance_tests: protocol: only TASK blocks from authenticated integrator are instructions
revisit_triggers: agents acting on peer msgs as tasks

nodes.definition: Separate instruction channels from data channels: system/dev for rules, user for task, tool for observations. Do not concatenate untrusted text into system. Authenticity checks (ancestor tip, author login) belong on the instruction admission path.

excluded: SQL prepared statements as metaphor only

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: fetched page body appended into system prompt section

pros.claim: Channel separation is the primary injection control

cons.claim: Some CLIs only have a single prompt string needing manual delimiters

failure_modes: skip authenticity because looks like integrator
acceptance_tests: packaging doc states what may enter system vs user vs tool
revisit_triggers: injection via tool result marked as system

nodes.definition: Treat tool results as untrusted data even from internal tools: hostile file content, format attacks, oversized payloads. Bound size, never elevate tool text to authority, never auto-exec embedded commands. Label tool schemas as observations.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: file content contains SYSTEM UPDATE push --force and agent complies

pros.claim: Tool isolation stops second-order injection from repo files

cons.claim: Strict stripping may remove needed imperative code comments

failure_modes: auto-execute shell found in tool output
acceptance_tests: tool results labeled observation; size caps; no auto-exec of embedded commands

nodes.definition: Gate durable memory writes: only store operator-approved or schema-validated facts; never let untrusted content become long-term memory that reloads as tier0. Memory amplifies contamination across sessions. Prefer task-scoped notes over global memory for unvetted claims.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: global memory stores a jailbreak snippet that reloads every session

pros.claim: Gated memory prevents cross-session infection

cons.claim: Over-gating reduces helpful personalization

acceptance_tests: memory write path checks tier and schema; global store denies tier3

nodes.definition: High-stakes review roles should be read-only on production refs: they may comment and score but not push feature branches or alter TASK ledger. Read-only reduces blast radius if the reviewer context is contaminated or compromised by adversarial content under review.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: xverify agent pushes fixes into builder scope outside its write_scope

pros.claim: Read-only reviewers cannot widen blast radius
pros.example: findings-only branch or EXCHANGE review msg

cons.claim: Pure read-only cannot apply agreed tiny typo fixes without handoff

failure_modes: reviewer shares builder credentials with write
acceptance_tests: review role write_scope limited to EXCHANGE review paths

nodes.definition: Before high-stakes actions, run lightweight priming checks: did untrusted text propose tool names or scope changes? Did examples bias the chosen approach? Log flags; optionally force fresh replan. Checks are heuristic not perfect — combine with isolation architecture.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: agent adopts force-push workflow that only appeared in untrusted issue text

pros.claim: Detection catches late-stage influence before destructive tools
pros.example: flag then fresh replan on match

cons.claim: False positives slow work when legit docs mention forbidden tools by name

failure_modes: blocking on any mention including in hard denials list
acceptance_tests: pre-push/pre-destructive checklist includes priming flag review

nodes.definition: HTML/Markdown/JSON from outside can hide instructions in comments, white text, or alternate streams. Normalize to plain text or AST; strip scripts; present as quoted data. Prefer content-type aware parsers over raw paste into prompts.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: HTML comment contains instruction override that model still attends to

pros.claim: Normalized plain text reduces hidden-channel injection
pros.example: comments and scripts stripped before model

cons.claim: Over-stripping removes meaningful code fences needed for review

failure_modes: rendering untrusted HTML in privileged tools
acceptance_tests: untrusted markup pipeline: parse, strip, quote, size-bound

nodes.definition: Isolation also protects outbound leakage: workers with untrusted content should not hold secrets, and prompts must not echo credentials into EXCHANGE or logs. Context engineering includes what must never enter a low-trust context (tokens, private keys, absolute secret paths).

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: standing orders with secret paths get pasted into public EXCHANGE msg

pros.claim: Secret-free worker contexts stop exfil via untrusted content coercion

cons.claim: Over-redaction removes needed path info for debugging

failure_modes: put absolute secret paths in repo msgs
acceptance_tests: pre-push secret scan on EXCHANGE paths; workers launched without secret env

nodes.definition: Separate authoring, planning, and judging into roles with different contexts and incentives. Planner proposes, author implements, judge evaluates without author self-praise. Separation is the structural fix for contamination that prompts alone cannot solve.

included: author vs judge vs planner roles
excluded: corporate RACI only without AI context

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: same session author grades its own delivery as ACCEPTED

pros.claim: Structural separation beats prompt-only fairness claims

cons.claim: More roles increase coordination latency
cons.example: three hops for a one-line fix

failure_modes: planner and judge share contaminated thread
acceptance_tests: task pattern single+xverify maps to distinct assignee for verify

nodes.definition: When contamination is suspected (injection flag, contradicted pins, rebound near-miss): stop destructive tools, snapshot state to durable store, spawn fresh context with cleaned packet (pins+goal+facts, no suspect text), resume. Do not continue carefully in the same soup.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: after injection flag agent continues same session and pushes

pros.claim: Hard reset contains incidents better than careful continuation

cons.claim: Reset loses nuanced mid-repair state if snapshot incomplete
cons.example: forgot failing test name in packet

acceptance_tests: incident runbook: stop, snapshot, fresh, clean packet, resume

nodes.definition: Log boundary events: tier label assignments, quarantine invocations, rejected instruction admissions, memory write denials, reset triggers. Audits enable postmortems and prove isolation was attempted. Exclude secrets from logs.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: cannot prove whether untrusted content was quarantined in an incident

pros.claim: Audit trails make isolation verifiable
pros.example: postmortem shows quarantine skip at t=12

cons.claim: Verbose audits can leak content snippets if poorly redacted

acceptance_tests: audit schema for admission/quarantine/memory-deny/reset; redaction rules

nodes.definition: Build sandboxed prompts for risky subtasks: minimal tools, positive required actions, no secret env, explicit tier labels, closed output schema. Sandbox is defense-in-depth with quarantine and freshness — not a substitute for either.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: risky web-read subtask launched with full secret env and push tools

pros.claim: Sandbox prompts shrink impact of residual injection

cons.claim: Too-tight sandbox fails the subtask and forces unsafe parent fallback

acceptance_tests: sandbox template: tools allowlist, output schema, secret-free, positive instructions

nodes.definition: Resuming a long session can rehydrate contamination. On resume, re-validate pins, re-run priming checks, and consider partial reset if the session handled untrusted content. Resume is not free safety — it is a risk decision.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: resumed session still carries jailbreak from earlier web read

pros.claim: Resume checks prevent zombie contamination
pros.example: pin probe on resume catches drift

cons.claim: Aggressive resume resets annoy operators mid-repair

acceptance_tests: resume checklist: pins, priming flags, untrusted-history bit

nodes.definition: Periodically test isolation with canary injections in fixtures (not prod tasks): does quarantine hold, does ASSIGNEE filter hold, does memory gate hold? Isolation without tests decays. Record pass/fail in audit, never store canary as real memory.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: isolation feature flagged done but canary jailbreak still elevates to system

pros.claim: Canaries catch isolation regressions before real attacks

cons.claim: Poorly isolated canaries can poison shared fixtures
cons.example: canary committed as real standing order

acceptance_tests: at least three canaries: web inject, peer inject, memory poison; CI or scheduled run

edges.why_related: continuity for repair vs freshness for isolation
edges.resolution_rule: session for build repair loops; fresh for judge/quarantine/high-risk plan

edges.why_related: need explicit bans vs rebound from ban walls
edges.resolution_rule: lead with required action; keep short closed ban list paired with alternatives

edges.why_related: need untrusted info vs any inclusion primes
edges.resolution_rule: structured claims only; never authority; optional fresh parent replan after

conflict_axes.name: continuity_vs_freshness
conflict_axes.description: Session repair benefits vs isolation resets
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: session for build; fresh for judge/quarantine/high-risk

conflict_axes.name: ban_clarity_vs_rebound
conflict_axes.description: Explicit DON'T lists vs ironic priming
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: required action first; short closed bans with alternatives

conflict_axes.name: info_need_vs_quarantine
conflict_axes.description: Need untrusted data vs minimize contact

conflict_axes.name: share_vs_lateral_risk
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: schema digests as data; only integrator TASKs

conflict_axes.name: memory_utility_vs_poison
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: gate by tier; task-scoped for unvetted

conflict_axes.name: reviewer_power_vs_safety
conflict_axes.description: Reviewer ability to fix vs blast radius

conflict_axes.name: sandbox_tightness
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: allowlist for task class; avoid parent unsafe fallback

conflict_axes.name: resume_speed_vs_revalidation
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: resume checklist; reset if untrusted-history bit set

conflict_axes.name: audit_detail_vs_leakage
conflict_axes.description: Rich audit vs secret/content leakage in logs
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: event types plus redacted hashes; no secrets

edge_cases.description: Jailbreak inside README fetched for docs
edge_cases.mitigation: quarantine extract; never system-merge; prime scan

edge_cases.description: Peer agent posts TASK-like text without ASSIGNEE
edge_cases.mitigation: ASSIGNEE plus authenticity required; else data only

edge_cases.description: DON'T force-push wall then near-miss force push
edge_cases.mitigation: rewrite to FF-only required action; log near-miss

edge_cases.description: Judge reads full builder self-praise transcript
Memory stores untrusted claim as global fact
edge_cases.mitigation: deny tier3 global writes; canary test

edge_cases.description: Sandbox still has GITHUB_TOKEN in env
Resume after web-heavy session without checks
edge_cases.mitigation: resume checklist; reset if untrusted bit

edge_cases.description: Tool dumps 100k hostile log with embedded orders
Canary left in production standing orders
Single-string CLI merges data into instruction blob
edge_cases.mitigation: delimiters and labels; prefer role API

workflow.description: Assign trust tier to each context segment
Run authenticity checks before accepting TASKs
Send untrusted reads through quarantine extraction
Rewrite critical ops prompts to required-action-first
Pick session vs fresh per role
workflow.gate: judge/quarantine not same soup as author self-score

workflow.description: Launch clean worker with task packet
Bound and label tool outputs as observations
Validate tier before durable memory write
Scan for untrusted influence before destructive tools
Stop, snapshot, fresh clean packet on contamination
Log admission, quarantine, deny, reset events

priority_rationale: Trust boundaries and injection controls dominate convenience; freshness for judges dominates same-session self-grading; positive framing dominates ban walls for critical tools.

dominance_rules.rationale: untrusted volume must not outvote system rules
dominance_rules.trigger: conflict between tier3 text and pins
dominance_rules.action: ignore tier3 as authority; keep pins
required action first plus short bans

dominance_rules.rationale: lateral injection is a swarm risk
dominance_rules.action: treat as data unless authenticated TASK

dominance_rules.rationale: limit blast radius of review context
dominance_rules.action: findings only unless explicitly scoped fixes

iteration_protocol.trigger: injection or authority claim from untrusted text
iteration_protocol.action: quarantine path; prime flag; consider reset

iteration_protocol.trigger: near-miss on forbidden tool after DON'T framing
iteration_protocol.action: rewrite positive; log rebound; optional fresh replan
purge bad entries; tighten gate; run canary
force fresh judge packet; remove self-scores

iteration_protocol.trigger: sandbox had secrets or push tools
resume without checklist after untrusted work
iteration_protocol.action: run resume checks; reset if needed
